QF.id: SIA Logic Model for Social Programs_1

question.text: Ms. Sunita Patil (CA and empanelled SIA) is reviewing the project design documents of Pragati Foundation, an NPO listed on NSE-SSE under the 'promoting education' eligible activity. The documents include a Logical Framework Analysis (LFA). For the SIA, what is the PRIMARY purpose of the LFA during her scoping exercise?

answer.text: To provide the basis for calculating the SROI ratio required under SAS-1400
To list the donors and the donations received during the financial year
To replace the statutory audit under Section 12AB of the Income Tax Act

To provide a structured tool that breaks the project into clearly defined components linking inputs, activities, outputs, outcomes and impact so the project can be planned, implemented, monitored and evaluated coherently

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook describes LFA as a systematic and structured tool widely used for project planning, implementation, monitoring and evaluation, organizing objectives, activities, and outcomes. The matrix components cover impact, outcomes, outputs, activities, and inputs, allowing the project's design to be read coherently end to end. The Trap: Treating LFA as just an SROI input, a donor register, or a substitute for statutory tax audit confuses the LFA with downstream computations or unrelated compliance tools. Note: Because the LFA links inputs through to outcomes and impact, it is a natural starting point when scoping an assessment, even though the matrix itself is a design and management tool rather than a compliance certificate.
